sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Garun Pal Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rahul Kumar Sharma
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

Heard Sri Garun Pal Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rahul Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
2. Applicant seeks bail in Complaint Case No. 495 of 2022, U/S 307, 376 IPC, Police Station Mursaan, District Hathras, during the pendency of trial.

PROSECUTION STORY:
3. The applicant is stated to have committed rape with the wife of the informant on 12.6.2022 at about 6.00 pm in the field by pointing country-made pistol on her chest.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF THE APPLICANT:
Ravendra Singh vs State Of U.P. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41243995/
1 4.

entities.text: Ravendra Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
5. The instant case is filed after a delay of four days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
6. There is no medical report to corroborate the prosecution story.
The victim is a married lady.
7. The instant case is a counterblast to the Case Crime No. 203 of 2009 u/s 364 IPC, in which the trial is still going on.
8. The applicant has a criminal history of one case, which has been explained, as the said offence is bailable.
9. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 16.6.2024.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT/STATE:
10. The bail application of the applicant have been opposed but the aforesaid submissions of learned counsel for the applicant have not been disputed.
CONCLUSION:
11. In the case of Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, (2020) 11 SCC 648, the Supreme Court has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused by itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail.
12. In so far as criminal antecedents of the applicant is concerned, it is not the case of the State that applicant might tamper with or otherwise adversely influence the investigation, or that he might intimidate witnesses before or during the trial.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, (2020) 11 SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The State has also not placed any material that applicant in past attempted to evade the process of law.

If the accused is otherwise found to be entitled to bail, he cannot be denied bail only on the ground of criminal history, no exceptional circumstances on the basis of criminal antecedents have been shown to deny bail to accused, hence,
the Court does not feel it proper to deny bail to the applicant just on the ground that he had criminal antecedent.
13. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

Ravendra Singh vs State Of U.P. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41243995/
2 14.

entities.text: Ravendra Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
15.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasized that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
16. Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
17. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

18. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant- Ravendra Singh involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
20. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

21. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the Ravendra Singh vs State Of U.P. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41243995/
